history.note: Every All-Star Game we have a usable record for. The scatter across years IS the uncertainty — an exhibition total is not a tight quantity. The 2026 game is in this table now, added from the graded box score after the projection had already been fitted on the 21 games that existed then. It ran the fastest of the 22 at 1.3185 times league pace and scored 251. It does NOT enter the comparable-format average. 2026 was played without free throws, which is the same reason 2022, 2023 and 2025 are set aside, so that average is unchanged at 18 games and 1.2065 — the most extreme game on record does not move the basis we fit on. We re-ran the finding that All-Star pace has not moved in 27 years with 2026 included and it held: the era contrast went from p=0.93 to p=0.67, still nowhere near significant.
history.reference: All-Star Game results and box scores, joined to each season's league-average pace.

sample.effective_n_note: The record holds 22 All-Star Games. The format has changed repeatedly, so the effective sample inside any single format is single digits — which is exactly why the intervals on this page are wide. The projection was fitted on the 5 drafted-format games played before 2026, and that basis has not been refitted.
notes: Years with no All-Star Game: 2004 (Olympic break (Athens)), 2008 (Olympic break (Beijing)), 2010 (FIBA World Championship year - no ASG held), 2012 (Olympic break (London)), 2016 (Olympic break (Rio)), 2020 (COVID-19 / season disruption)

Pace is measured as a multiplier on the same season's league-average pace, not in absolute terms — the league itself has sped up a lot since 1999, and the ratio removes that confound without spending anything to do it.
2022/2023/2025 use a NO-FREE-THROWS all-star format; FTA under-records shooting fouls so their 0.4*FTA possession term is biased LOW. Use mean_comparable_only unless you model that bias explicitly.

sources.reference: All-Star Game results and box scores joined to season league pace.

why_tighter.finding: This is a RESULT, not an inconsistency.
why_tighter.plain: Pace varies 3.3x LESS than efficiency across drafted-format games. About 91% of the uncertainty in the total comes from how EFFICIENT the game is, only ~9% from how FAST it is. A tight pace band next to a wide total band is exactly what the same finding that pace is flat predicts -- forcing them to look alike would hide the result.

headline.finding: ALL-STAR BASKETBALL IS BOTH FASTER AND EASIER THAN THE REGULAR SEASON -- but the 27-YEAR SCORING EXPLOSION IS ENTIRELY EFFICIENCY, NOT TEMPO.
points: Pace runs ~1.28x league in the drafted-teams format (1.22x across all 21 games). All-Star basketball IS substantially faster than regular-season play -- tempo is a large part of WHY the total is high.

But tempo has not MOVED. The era contrast on the pace multiplier is beta=+0.0034, p=0.93 -- indistinguishable from zero across 27 years. Points per possession went 0.848 -> 1.355 (beta=+0.176, p=0.009). The RISE in All-Star scoring is the disappearance of defense.

alternatives.note: The same record answers this question three ways depending on which games you are willing to call comparable. We ship the format-matched one; the others are shown so the choice is visible rather than hidden.
alternatives.shipped: S over the 5 captain_draft games (2026's actual format)

scenario.title: An unconfirmed rule that would change everything
scenario.text: A target-score / Elam ending is single-sourced (PrizePicks), uncorroborated, and arithmetically incompatible with its own posted total (Elam +8 implies ~225-235, 45-55 BELOW every market line). Treated as a LABELLED TAIL only, not baked into the distribution. If an Elam ending is in fact used, the total collapses toward the ~225-235 region and this projection is wrong on the low-probability branch.
scenario.extra: 4-point line and hockey-style substitutions are CONFIRMED for 2025 but UNRELEASED for 2026. Not baked in; they widen the interval upward rather than moving the median.

rules.name: drafted teams format
rules.basis: Negligible on total scoring. The 2025 game was also a drafted-captains format and produced a record 282 combined points, so drafting per se is not a scoring lever. Possible small teammate-chemistry effect: Team Spoon has three same-club pairs (Clark/Boston - Fever, Miles/C.Williams - Lynx, Gray/R.Howard - Dream) while Team Coop has none. GUESS: worth at most ~1-2 points of margin to Spoon, not to the total.

rules.name: exhibition defensive intensity
rules.basis: Baseline expectation ~275-285 combined over a full 40 minutes, consistent with the market (DraftKings 275.5, SI 277.5, Sports Interaction 276.5, PrizePicks 279.5; opened 274.5). MEASURABLE from the 2022/2023/2025 series plus the +5.1 ppg league-wide scoring rise.

rules.name: target score elam ending
rules.basis: IF TRUE, this is enormous and negative for the total. Working the arithmetic off 2025 (282 combined over 40 minutes, ~70.5 combined points per quarter, ~113 for the leader after three quarters): target ~121, final ~121-108, i.e. ~225-235 combined -- roughly 45-55 points BELOW the posted market total of 275.5-279.5. The gap between the reported rule and the market price is itself the strongest evidence the rule report is WRONG, because a real target-score ending would have moved every book. TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED. Recommended disposition: model the full-40-minute case as the primary and carry the Elam case only as a labelled tail scenario.

rules.name: four point shot
rules.basis: IF carried over from 2025: GUESS roughly +4 to +10 combined points versus no 4-point line, from a modest number of attempts at +1 point each. If it is not in play, zero. Since it cannot be confirmed either way, do not bake it into a point estimate -- widen the scoring interval upward instead.

rules.name: live hockey style substitutions
rules.basis: GUESS: raises possessions by removing dead-ball stoppages. Order of a few extra possessions per team, worth maybe +3 to +8 combined points if in play. Zero if not. Unconfirmed -- do not bake in.

rules.name: thirtieth season celebration
rules.basis: GUESS: no measurable effect on pace or scoring. Ceremonial. Possible second-order effect only if pregame ceremony compresses warmups or lengthens stoppages -- unmeasurable, treat as zero.

rules.name: charity and bonus stakes
rules.basis: GUESS: real money on the outcome can raise late-game competitive intensity, which historically SUPPRESSES scoring slightly (more defense in the closing minutes) while raising variance. Effect on the total: unclear, plausibly -3 to +0 combined points. Not measurable from the available history.

rules.name: skills or three point contest carryover
rules.basis: Zero. No carryover mechanism exists per the available sources.

players.note: Ordered by our un-adjusted season impact rating. This table used to be ordered by an exhibition-adjusted impact that discounted defence; that adjustment has been measured since the game and withdrawn (see the correction at the top), so the column is gone rather than re-weighted. Offense share is kept as a plain description of how a player's box-score production splits — it no longer scales anything. Minutes are flattened, which compresses every counting projection. Counting stats sit last on purpose.
players.reference: Our season impact ratings, shown as they were fitted, with no exhibition re-weighting applied.

The shaded bands hold the middle of that record, the highlighted line is the split this page published, and anything left of the even-split line is a night the reserves played more.

Read it as close: the gap is 0.6 spread over eleven players a side, and we would not call that a verdict.

fun.title: Haul verdict: the two measures disagree
fun.text: Reputation says Team Coop (mean draft slot 10.7 against 12.3). Un-adjusted season impact says Team Spoon (7.0 against 6.4). They point at different sides. The earlier verdict on this page, that the same team won both, was reached through the withdrawn exhibition adjustment and no longer stands.

fun.title: Withdrawn: the claim that the regime flipped the haul
fun.text: We published that once defence is discounted for an exhibition, the side with the better haul changes. That claim depended entirely on an assumed defensive weight of 0.35, which we flagged at the time as the number to distrust. With the 2026 game played we measured it across six drafted-format All-Star Games and 132 player-games: defensive production carries over better than offensive production, not worse. The claim needed the weight below about 0.94 to hold and every measurement puts it far above. There is no flip. Withdrawn rather than restated with a different number, because the honest replacement is that we do not have one.

fun_caveat: CORRECTED AFTER THE GAME. These cards used to turn on an exhibition adjustment that weighted defensive contribution at 0.35 and offensive at 1.25. That weighting was asserted, never fitted, and the page said so. It has since been measured against six drafted-format All-Star Games and it did not hold. Every card below now reads on un-adjusted season ratings, and the one finding that could not survive without the adjustment has been withdrawn outright.
fun_note: Disclosing an assumption was the right thing to do while it was still only an assumption. It stopped being enough the moment we measured it and it failed, so this is a correction rather than a caveat.
assumptions: CHEMISTRY IS NEUTRALIZED OUTRIGHT -- set to exactly zero, not estimated. Drafted teams have no shared lineup history; any chemistry term fitted here is noise.
IMPACT RATINGS ARE APPLIED OUTSIDE THE REGIME THEY WERE FIT IN. our published player ratings ratings are fit on regular-season WNBA play and are being used on an exhibition.

WITHDRAWN, 2026-07-29 -- EXHIBITION REGIME ADJUSTMENT: defensive share weighted 0.35x, offensive share 1.25x. This was asserted, not estimated. It has since been measured across six drafted-format All-Star Games and it did not hold -- defensive production carried over better than offensive, not worse. The adjustment is no longer applied anywhere on this page and no replacement value has been substituted in its place.
DEFENSIVE SHARE IS A BOX-SCORE PROXY (stl/blk/reb vs pts/ast), z-scored within the All-Star pool. It is NOT a defensive RAPM. Real defensive impact is not separable from the ratings available.
MINUTES ARE FLATTENED: 85% equal-split of 200 team-minutes + 15% starter tilt. Regular-season minute distributions do NOT apply to an All-Star Game.
Total points modelled on S = total/(2*league_pace_per40), which is invariant to the free-throw possession bias. The pace-vs-efficiency split is NOT invariant to it.
Margin sign is not predicted -- only a higher side and a lower side.
League 1999-2014 pace inputs are 'estimated_calibrated', not measured; that uncertainty is NOT propagated into the intervals.
Era contrast on PACE -- tested, did not survive the power check; pace uses its mean.
Chemistry -- zeroed by assumption.
Rule effects -- carried verbatim from the rosters file as named lines with is_guess flags; NOT re-estimated and NOT silently summed into the total.
Per-player variance / player-level intervals -- not estimable at this n.
Margin sign / which team wins -- not modelled.

assumptions.name: Chemistry is neutralized outright
assumptions.text: These are drafted sides with no shared history. Any chemistry term fitted here would be noise dressed as signal, so it is set to zero by assumption rather than estimated.

assumptions.name: Ratings are used outside the regime they were fit in
assumptions.text: Player impact ratings were fit on regular-season basketball. An All-Star exhibition is a different game. Every player line is directional only.

assumptions.name: Minutes are flattened
assumptions.text: All-Star minutes are spread far more evenly than a regular-season rotation, which compresses every counting projection relative to a normal night.

assumptions.name: Defense is discounted, offense is upweighted
assumptions.text: Exhibition defense is not played at regular-season intensity. Defensive impact is discounted and offensive impact carries more of the read.

assumptions.name: The width is the finding
assumptions.text: A tight interval on an exhibition would be evidence of a bug, not of skill. Read the band, not the tick.

draft_disagreement.lede: For every drafted All-Star we compare where they actually went in the draft to where our on-court impact rating would have taken them, ranked within the same group of players. A bar to the right means the draft let them slide past where we rate them; a bar to the left means the draft took them earlier than our rating would have.
draft_disagreement.note: Our rating is a regular-season on-court impact number being used outside the regime it was fit in, and an honorary GM drafting a televised exhibition is not solving the same problem we are. This is a conversation, not a scorecard. The two top fan vote-getters were placed by coin flip rather than drafted, so they have no draft slot to disagree with.

read_this_first: THIS IS AN EXHIBITION. Every rating and every per-minute rate used here was fit on REGULAR-SEASON play and is being applied OUT OF REGIME to an All-Star game. Nothing below is a regular-season-grade projection.
The team total this all hangs off rests on n=5 format-matched games. Player level is thinner still. The WIDTH IS THE FINDING -- a tight prop is a manufactured prop.
Odds shown are FAIR (zero vig). A real book will price worse on both sides. An edge only exists if the book's price beats the fair price by more than its hold.
Betting is a DOWNSTREAM READOUT of the impact/rating model and the team projection -- read those first, these second.
Kelsey Plum is OUT. Kahleah Copper is her replacement and was NOT drafted (no pick slot).
STL / BLK / TOV are NOT offered: the All-Star box-score record carries no steal, block or turnover columns, so there is no All-Star basis to calibrate them against. UNKNOWN, not guessed.

assumptions: Impact ratings and per-minute rates are applied OUT OF REGIME (regular season -> exhibition).
Chemistry is neutralised outright (zero), per the team projection -- drafted teams, no shared history.

The exhibition regime shows up here as an OFFENCE-ONLY share driver: point/rebound/assist shares are driven by offensive per-minute production, and defensive value contributes nothing to a player's share. That IS the defensive discount at the player level.
Minute-distribution SHAPE is fitted from real All-Star box scores; player-to-slot ASSIGNMENT is asserted.
Share dispersion is fitted CONSERVATIVELY WIDE: historical per-minute rate differences are folded into the residual, so simulated prop distributions are wider than truth rather than tighter.
Margin sign is not predicted -- only a higher and a lower side, resampled from captain_draft margins.
Full 40 minutes assumed. If the disputed target-score / Elam ending is real, every number here is too high (the team projection puts that branch 45-55 combined points lower).
A 4-point line (unconfirmed for 2026) would raise scoring props; not baked in.

retraction.headline: Correction: we have withdrawn the comparison of which side drafted better
lines: Before the game we published a comparison of the two hauls that leaned on one number we made up rather than measured: we assumed a defensive contribution is worth 0.35 of an offensive one in an exhibition. We said on this page that it was an assumption and the largest single choice in the model.

The game has now been played. It was the sixth All-Star Game played under drafted teams, which was the point we had committed in advance to stop asserting that number and measure it instead, across 132 player-games. We measured it. It did not hold, and it was not even wrong in the expected direction: defensive production carried over from the regular season BETTER than offensive production did, which is the opposite of a discount.

So the finding that rested on it is withdrawn. We had published that discounting defence flipped which captain drafted better. For that to be true the defensive weight had to be below about 0.94; every way we can measure it puts it well above. There is no flip. One side leads on the un-adjusted ratings and still leads on any adjustment we can defend.

We are not replacing 0.35 with a new number. What we are able to measure is not quite the thing 0.35 was trying to be, and the only defensive statistic the historical All-Star box scores carry is total rebounds. We would rather show the un-adjusted season ratings and say plainly what they are than swap one unfitted constant for a bigger one.

This does not touch the forecast. The game finished 251 against our published median of 261.3 — the result landed at the 34th percentile of our own published distribution, our 80% range held, and we were closer than every posted market total. Our finding that All-Star pace has been flat for 27 years also survives the new game, even though 2026 was the fastest All-Star Game on record. This correction is about one comparison, not the projection.
retraction.reference: Graded against a plan written down before tip-off.

result.headline: Team Spoon 129, Team Coop 122
lines: Team Spoon won the 2026 All-Star Game 129-122. The two sides combined for 251 points.
Jonquel Jones led everyone in points, rebounds and assists combined for Team Spoon: 22 points, 13 rebounds and 8 assists.
Kelsey Mitchell led all scorers for Team Coop, with 28 points, 4 rebounds and 2 assists.

Before the game we published a median of 261.3 combined points, in a range we said was the finding. The game finished 251. That is the 34th percentile of the distribution we published, inside our own 80 percent range.

One piece of it missed: we had the game running about 1.28 times league pace and it ran 1.32, the fastest All-Star Game on record and just past the top edge of our band. The scoring came in below our median anyway, because the shooting was cooler than we had it.
Every posted total was further from the result than ours was.
result.played: Played July 25 at the United Center in Chicago.
result.reference: Graded against a plan written down before the game.
